newsitem.title: USA: Batterer charged in NY decapitations, other killing.
newsitem.headline: Batterer charged in NY decapitations, other killing.

text.p: A subway cleaner with a history of battering has been charged with decapitating his wife and their son and killing the boy's half-brother, authorities said on Tuesday.
Richard Timmons, 33, was charged with first- and second-degree murder in connection with the killings, Queens District Attorney's office spokeswoman Mary de Bourbon said.

Timmons, who had pleaded guilty to assaulting his wife Annita Stewart Timmons, a 33-year-old hospital clerk, had been freed from jail 10 days before the bloody slayings that left even veteran police investigators shaken.

Despite his history of attacks, Annita Timmons had admitted him to her apartment at a public housing project. She had a limited court order of protection that still allowed her husband to have contact with her.

Police allege Timmons assaulted his wife and family late on Sunday, cut off his wife's head and that of his son Aaron, 7, and fatally stabbed Aaron's half-brother, Sharrone, 13. He then slashed his own wrists in an apparent suicide attempt.
Aaron was heard pleading for mercy when he called the 911 emergency number during the attack. "Daddy, stop it!" he shouted. Police recovered a kitchen knife and hatchet from the apartment.

De Bourbon said Timmons had pleaded guilty to assault and other charges stemming from 1996 attacks on his wife. He was released after nine months in jail. Prosecutors objected to his release and argued for a stronger order of protection.
"We felt she should have had an order that would have kept him from going anywhere near her," she said.
